# Preparing UNICEF data {#c03-prepare-unicef}

[Organising the UNICEF download](#c01-organise) unpacks the country files and, if the harmonisation scripts are present, writes the AFLEARN analysis files. This chapter explains what those files contain and how to extend them.

The UNICEF route produces a child-level analysis file in three steps:

```text
organised country folders
        │
        ▼
merge files within a country, if you need variables the scripts do not already attach
        │
        ▼
harmonised selected-child file
        +
research-ready reading file
```

`run-it.R` already sources `harmonize-mics-fs-v1.0.R` and `harmonize-mics-reading-v1.1.R`. The pages that follow show how to re-run one of those steps, what the output variables mean, and how to merge additional source files by hand when the research question needs them.

Decide what one row of the final dataset represents before merging anything. For foundational-learning research, one row is usually the selected child in `fs`. [Files, units of observation and identifiers](#c02-files) sets out the keys; this chapter shows the code.

If you started from IPUMS instead, go to [Preparing IPUMS data](#c04-prepare-ipums).
